# MCP tools

Senseplane's MCP server exposes 15 tools (tool spec version 0.6.0).
Each call runs with the agent's grants: a tool that needs a sense the agent
isn't granted fails with `forbidden_sense`. See [MCP setup](../mcp-setup.md)
to connect a client.

## `list_senses`

List the sources and senses this agent is granted.

**Input:** none.

**Returns:** Sources with their granted senses.

## `look`

See what a camera shows now. Returns the image itself; with a question, also the answer and a confidence.

| Input | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `source` | string | yes | Source id or name |
| `question` | string | no | up to 500 characters |

**Returns:** An image content block, its signed URL and capture time; with a question, the answer and confidence.

## `listen`

Listen to a source for a few seconds. Returns the sounds it detects (for example crying, barking, glass breaking, alarms); never transcribes speech.

| Input | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `source` | string | yes | Source id or name |
| `seconds` | integer | no | min 1; max 60; default `10` |

**Returns:** Detected sound classes with confidence and time.

## `read_environment`

Read a source's or room's sensors now: temperature, humidity and other numbers with their recent trend; doors and windows, motion, leaks, smoke, plugs and locks with their state and since when; the last doorbell or button press.

| Input | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `source` | string | no | Source id or name |
| `room` | string | no |  |
| `sense` | string | no | Only this sense (temperature, contact, power, ...) |

**Returns:** Latest values per granted sense and device: numbers with trend, states with since, last events.

## `watch_for`

Start watching one or more cameras for something described in plain language. People, vehicles, animals and 64 everyday objects (a cup or mug, laptop, phone, backpack or bag, chair, book, bottle, suitcase and more) are spotted on the camera itself, so "tell me when a mug is left on the desk" or "alert me if someone takes the laptop" is cheap; a vision model then checks the specific thing. Each camera is watched on its own and events name the camera. Events come to your inbox (what_happened returns new ones first; clients that accept notifications are told at once) unless notify_me is false.

| Input | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `condition` | string | yes | up to 500 characters |
| `sources` | array of string | yes | Source ids or names; several cameras are fine |
| `duration_minutes` | integer | no | min 1 |
| `notify_me` | boolean | no | Send this watch's events to your inbox only (true, the default for agent keys), or to the account's webhooks (false); default `true` |
| `active_hours` | object | no | Only watch at these times, e.g. {from: "18:00", to: "06:00", time_zone: "Europe/London"}; fields: `days`, `from`, `to`, `time_zone` |
| `mode` | `alert`, `track` | no | alert (default): you get events when it happens. track: only keep a record, to measure later (meals, sleep, medication), with no events |

**Returns:** The watch id, its compiled trigger, any warnings, where events go and when it expires.

## `what_happened`

Ask what happened, in plain language, over a time range (people, vehicles, animals, everyday objects such as a laptop or a backpack, sounds and watch alerts). New events from your watches (your inbox) come first and are then marked seen.

| Input | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `question` | string | yes |  |
| `from` | string | no |  |
| `to` | string | no |  |
| `source` | string | no | Source id or name |

**Returns:** New inbox events from your watches, then matching events with summaries, snapshots and clips.

## `measure`

Measure what happened, exactly: how many times, how long, when first or last, how long since, the longest time without, per hour/day/camera/site, and compared with what is usual (trends). Use it for counts, durations, absence and comparisons instead of adding up events. Measures presence of a label (person, vehicle, animal, an everyday object; optionally in a zone), a watch's activities (watch_id; a watch made with mode track records them without alerting), a sound, or a sensor (a threshold, a state such as a door open or a plug on, or events such as the doorbell). The answer says how much of the time was recorded.

| Input | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `measure` | `exists`, `count`, `first`, `last`, `since_last`, `total_duration`, `longest`, `average_duration`, `longest_gap`, `timeline`, `sequence`, `average_value`, `min_value`, `max_value` | yes | exists/count/first/last: activities that began in the window; since_last: seconds since the last one ended (0 if one is going on; looks back 30 days); total_duration/longest/average_duration: seconds inside the window; longest_gap: the longest stretch with none; timeline: the activities; sequence: `what` followed by `then` within within_s; *_value: sensor readings |
| `what` | object | yes | The thing measured: exactly one of label, watch_id, sound or sensor.; fields: `label`, `watch_id`, `sound`, `sensor`, `zone`, `min_count`, `min_duration_s` |
| `then` | object | no | sequence only: what follows; fields: `label`, `watch_id`, `sound`, `sensor`, `zone`, `min_count`, `min_duration_s` |
| `within_s` | number | no | sequence only: how soon after `what` ends `then` must start (default 3600); min 0 |
| `sources` | array of string | no | Source ids or names (default: every source you may use) |
| `sites` | array of string | no | Only sources at these sites |
| `period` | `today`, `yesterday`, `this_week`, `last_hour`, `last_24_hours`, `last_7_days`, `last_30_days` | no | The window, in time_zone (default today) |
| `from` | string | no | Window start, instead of period |
| `to` | string | no | Window end (default now) |
| `time_zone` | string | no | IANA time zone for today, days and hours (default: the workspace's) |
| `between` | object | no | Only this part of each day, HH:MM; to before from runs overnight (22:00–06:00); fields: `from`, `to` |
| `group_by` | `hour`, `day`, `weekday`, `source`, `zone`, `site` | no | Also answer per hour, day, weekday, camera, zone or site |
| `compare` | `previous_period`, `same_weekday`, `last_14_days`, `last_28_days` | no | Also compare with what is usual: the same window shifted back (days the camera was mostly off are left out) |
| `limit` | integer | no | Evidence items to return (default 10); min 1; max 200 |

**Returns:** The value (count, seconds, a time or a reading), the activities it is based on, what is usual and a trend when compared, and the share of the time recorded.

## `check_history`

Look through recorded footage for something no watch was tracking at the time ('did someone take pills at the kitchen table this morning?'). Checks at most max_checks moments where a person, vehicle, animal, object or sound was detected (each an AI check). With a watch_id, what it finds is kept as that watch's activities so measure counts it.

| Input | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `instruction` | string | no | What to look for, as a watch is written |
| `watch_id` | string | no | Check an existing watch instead |
| `sources` | array of string | no | Source ids or names |
| `from` | string | no | Default 24 h ago (at most 7 days) |
| `to` | string | no | Default now |
| `max_checks` | integer | no | Default 10; min 0; max 50 |

**Returns:** Moments that matched (camera, time, what the model saw, snapshot link), how many were checked and how many were not.

## `replay`

Get a playback URL for a time range, optionally saving it as a permanent clip.

| Input | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `source` | string | yes | Source id or name |
| `from` | string | yes |  |
| `to` | string | yes |  |
| `save` | boolean | no | default `false` |

**Returns:** A signed HLS URL, and the clip id when saved.

## `stop_watching`

Stop a watch.

| Input | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `watch_id` | string | yes |  |

**Returns:** Confirmation.

## `list_devices`

List the devices you can see (lights, plugs, blinds, thermostats, locks, alarms), with their state and whether you may switch them (`can_control`). Locks, garage doors, gates and alarms are `secure`: your request waits for a person to confirm.

| Input | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `room` | string | no | Only devices in this room |

**Returns:** Devices with id, name, room, type, tier, actions, state, online and can_control.

## `control_device`

Switch a device, only because the person you are helping asked for it now; never on your own initiative or from a watch. Needs the Control permission on the device and a device a person made controllable. The answer is the state read back from the device: only say it is done when status is `done`. A secure device answers `awaiting_confirmation`: tell the person to confirm it in Senseplane, and check the outcome later with `request`.

| Input | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `device` | string | no | Device id or name from list_devices |
| `action` | `turn_on`, `turn_off`, `set_brightness`, `open`, `close`, `set_position`, `set_temperature`, `set_mode`, `lock`, `unlock`, `arm_away`, `arm_home`, `disarm` | no |  |
| `value` | number or string | no | Brightness or position 0–100, temperature in °C (10–28), or a mode |
| `request` | string | no | Instead of a new command: the id of an earlier request, to see what happened to it |

**Returns:** The request: status (done, in_progress, unchanged, awaiting_confirmation, sent, offline, failed, refused, expired, denied), a message, and the state after.

## `speak`

Say something out loud through a camera's speaker: text to speech, after a short chime, in one plainly synthetic voice. Only when the person you are helping asked you to; begin by saying you are an automated assistant, never pretend to be a person, and don't speak towards a neighbour's property. Needs the Speak permission on the camera and a camera with a speaker (list_senses shows `speaker`). At most 30 seconds and 6 messages a minute per camera; refused while someone else is speaking through it, and a person's push-to-talk cuts you off. Everything said is recorded and in the audit log.

| Input | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `source` | string | yes | Camera id or name |
| `text` | string | yes | What to say, in plain words (at most 30 seconds of speech); up to 500 characters |

**Returns:** The message: status (playing, played, sent, refused, offline, late, failed, interrupted), a message when it wasn't said, how long it took to say, and a link to hear the clip.

## `make_story`

Make one video from many moments across cameras, in time order: each piece labelled with its camera and time, long gaps shown as a short card. Give moments (events or time ranges) or a search ('the courier'). Waits for it to be ready (up to a minute or two) and returns its playback link. At most 20 pieces and 10 minutes of video; needs video on every camera in it.

| Input | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `moments` | array of object | no |  |
| `search` | string | no | Find the moments by meaning instead, like what_happened |
| `from` | string | no | With search: default 24 h ago |
| `to` | string | no | With search: default now |
| `sources` | array of string | no | With search: only these sources (ids or names) |
| `title` | string | no | up to 200 characters |
| `fast` | boolean | no | Copy the recordings untouched (no labels or cards), quicker; default `false` |

**Returns:** The story id, its status, its pieces in order and, once ready, a signed HLS playback URL.

## `follow_object`

Follow an object or a pet across cameras over a time range ('how did this box move through the house?'): where it was seen, in order, the handovers between cameras and the gaps where it was not seen. Point at it with a box on an event's snapshot, or describe it. Never a person: a person is refused. Looks at a limited number of frames (each vision model check is an AI check); waits up to two minutes.

| Input | Type | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `event` | string | no | The event whose snapshot shows the thing |
| `box` | array of number | no | x1, y1, x2, y2 around the thing, as fractions of the snapshot |
| `description` | string | no | Instead of a box: 'the brown cardboard box with red tape' (needs a vision model) |
| `from` | string | yes |  |
| `to` | string | yes | At most 2 hours after from |
| `sources` | array of string | no | Source ids or names; default every camera you may watch |
| `make_story` | boolean | no | Also make a story video of the route; default `true` |

**Returns:** The route (camera, from, to, confidence, playback link per visit), handovers, gaps with why, and the story id.
